name: Anji Bai Cha
parentage: A rare, natural mutation discovered in the wild and then propagated.
description: 'Anji White Tea'. A unique and fascinating cultivar that, despite its name, is processed as a green tea. In the low temperatures of early spring, its leaves have an albino-like appearance due to a lack of chlorophyll. This results in an exceptionally high concentration of amino acids, producing a tea with a powerful, savory 'umami' flavor unlike any other green tea.
plantType: Delicate, temperature-sensitive bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Requires a specific microclimate with a cool spring to trigger its albino phase. It thrives in the bamboo-rich terroir of Anji County.
processing: Processing must be extremely gentle to protect the delicate, amino-acid-rich leaves. The goal is to do as little as possible to let the unique character of the raw material shine through.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are lightly steamed or pan-fired at a low temperature to halt oxidation while preserving their delicate structure and chemical composition.
roasting: No roasting. The tea is simply dried at a low temperature after the kill-green step. Any roasting would destroy its unique, savory flavor.
versatility: Extremely specialized. This cultivar is cultivated for one purpose only: to create the unique, umami-rich green tea known as Anji Bai Cha.

name: Asahi
parentage: Selected from the native Uji Zairai population.
description: 'Morning Sun'. An old and revered elite cultivar from Uji, Kyoto. It is considered one of the absolute highest-grade cultivars for Matcha production, prized for its supremely elegant, profoundly sweet, and umami-rich profile with almost no bitterness. It is often used for top-tier, ceremonial-grade Matcha.
plantType: Delicate, slow-growing, semi-upright bush with thin leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Requires the specific, stable, and rich terroir of Uji. It is a demanding cultivar with a low yield, reserved for the best plots.
processing: Asahi is a shading master. It must be shaded for an extended period (20+ days) to develop its unique chemical composition, which is high in L-theanine and low in catechins. The leaves are very delicate and must be handled with extreme care.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are lightly steamed immediately after harvest to preserve their delicate character.
roasting: No roasting. The leaves are processed into Tencha by being dried flat in a specialized 'tencha-ro' oven, which prepares them for stone-grinding without altering their pure flavor.
versatility: Extremely specialized. Asahi is a 'thoroughbred' cultivar used exclusively for producing the most premium, ceremonial-grade Matcha in Japan.

name: Asatsuyu
description: 'Morning Dew'. A legendary cultivar often referred to as a 'natural Gyokuro' due to its intense, sweet umami flavor, even when grown unshaded as Sencha. It is one of the parents of the elite Saemidori cultivar and is prized by connoisseurs for its powerful, savory, and sweet character, though it can be difficult to cultivate.

name: Ba Xian
parentage: Clonal selection from a Song Zhong mother tree.
description: 'Eight Immortals'. A powerful and assertive clonal Dan Cong cultivar, developed from eight cuttings of a venerable Song Zhong mother tree. It is renowned for its intense, almost aggressive fragrance and a strong, impactful flavor profile that sets it apart from more delicate floral types.
plantType: Vigorous arbor type with dark green, shiny leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the high-altitude, rocky terroir of the Phoenix Mountains, which provides the mineral foundation for its strong character.

name: Bai Ji Guan
parentage: One of the four original, legendary Wuyi cultivars, named for its unique appearance.
description: 'White Cockscomb'. A rare and unique member of the 'Si Da Ming Cong', Bai Ji Guan stands apart from all other Wuyi oolongs. It is named for its peculiar pale, yellowish-green leaves and is processed with a much lighter hand, resulting in a creamy, sweet, and custardy flavor profile that contrasts sharply with the dark, roasty character of its famous brethren.
plantType: Small, slow-growing, semi-upright bush with delicate branches (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Requires a specific microclimate within the Wuyi Mountains. It is less hardy than other Yancha cultivars and requires great care.
processing: Processing Bai Ji Guan requires immense skill and a light touch. The leaves are more fragile than other Wuyi cultivars, so the bruising and oxidation steps must be gentle to avoid bitterness and preserve its delicate aromatics.
oxidation: Oxidation is kept very light for a Yancha (20-30%). This preserves the leaf's natural pale color and its sweet, creamy, and corn-like flavor notes.
roasting: Roasting is minimal and done at a very low temperature. It is more of a final drying bake than a flavor-altering roast. The goal is to stabilize the tea while allowing its inherent sweetness and unique flavor to shine.
versatility: Extremely specialized. Bai Ji Guan represents a unique, almost historical style of light Yancha. It is not versatile and can only be made in this specific way.

name: Bai Wen
parentage: (Qing Xin Da Mao x TRES-1407)
description: 'White Hairs'. A modern cultivar developed by TRES specifically for the production of leafhopper-bitten teas like Oriental Beauty. It was designed to be a more productive and pest-resistant alternative to the traditional Qing Xin Da Mao cultivar, while still being able to produce the signature honey-fruit fragrance when bitten by the tea leafhopper.
plantType: Vigorous, upright bush with large, downy leaves.
environment: Grows well in the same hot, humid, and leafhopper-rich environments as Qing Xin Da Mao in northwestern Taiwan.
processing: Processing is identical to that of traditional Oriental Beauty. The key is that the leaves must be bitten by the tea leafhopper to initiate the chemical changes that create the unique aroma.
oxidation: Undergoes heavy oxidation (60-70%) to fully develop the complex honey and fruit flavors that result from the insect bites.
roasting: Completely unroasted. All the flavor and aroma are developed through the natural reaction to the insect bites and the subsequent heavy oxidation.
versatility: Extremely specialized. This cultivar was bred for the single purpose of making Oriental Beauty oolong, offering farmers a more reliable option.

name: Ban Tian Yao
parentage: Selected from the native Wuyi heirloom population.
description: 'Half-way to the Sky'. A classic Wuyi Rock Oolong named for the legend of its original bush growing halfway up a cliff. It is celebrated for its perfect balance and elegance, often described as the ideal middle-ground Yancha—lacking the sharp spice of Rou Gui or the deep woodiness of Shui Xian, it instead offers a clear, sweet, and floral profile.
plantType: Upright, medium-sized arbor type, well-adapted to rocky growth (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Best expresses itself in the core 'Zhengyan' region of the Wuyi Mountains, where the mineral-rich terroir contributes to its balanced flavor.
processing: The processing of Ban Tian Yao is a balancing act itself. The goal is not to impart extreme flavors but to reveal the cultivar's natural elegance. Its leaves are robust enough for traditional Yancha processing but shine when not pushed to extremes.
oxidation: Undergoes a standard medium-to-heavy oxidation for Yancha (40-60%) to develop a solid foundation of flavor that enhances its floral and fruity notes.
roasting: Typically receives a medium charcoal roast. This is enough to create the desired 'rock rhyme' and smoothness but light enough to preserve its delicate floral top notes, which could be lost with a heavier bake.
versatility: Highly specialized. Ban Tian Yao is a pure expression of the traditional Wuyi Rock Oolong style and is not used for other types of tea.

name: Bei Dou
altNames: North Star;Bei Dou Yi Hao (North Star #1)
parentage: Cloned from the Bei Dou mother tree, which itself was said to be a cutting from an original Da Hong Pao bush.
description: 'North Star'. A prestigious Wuyi Rock Oolong cultivar directly descended from the legendary Da Hong Pao lineage. It is renowned for its powerful and robust character, thick body, and a classic roasted flavor profile that is both complex and deeply satisfying, making it a favorite among seasoned Yancha drinkers.
plantType: Sturdy, upright arbor type well-adapted to rocky terrain (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows best in the core 'Zhengyan' region of the Wuyi Mountains, where the mineral-rich soil and terroir create its powerful flavor.
processing: The processing of Bei Dou is a classic example of traditional Yancha craftsmanship. Its strong leaves can withstand the necessary heavy oxidation and multiple roasts that build its complex character.
oxidation: Undergoes heavy oxidation (50-60%) to develop a rich, fruity, and robust flavor base that serves as the perfect foundation for the charcoal roasting process.
roasting: Receives a medium-to-heavy charcoal roast, often in multiple stages. This is essential for creating its signature roasted depth, smoothing its texture, and developing the long, sweet finish.
versatility: Highly specialized. Bei Dou is a pure expression of the traditional, powerful Wuyi Rock Oolong style and is not used for other types of tea.

name: Ben Shan
parentage: Close genetic relative of Tie Guan Yin, selected from the same Anxi heirloom population.
description: 'Original Mountain'. A close genetic relative of Tie Guan Yin from the neighboring mountains of Anxi. Ben Shan is known for producing a lighter-bodied oolong with a very clear, high-pitched floral aroma, often described as being more straightforward and less complex than its famous cousin. It is a popular and more affordable daily-drinker oolong.
plantType: Upright bush type, similar in appearance to Tie Guan Yin but slightly less robust (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in similar conditions to Tie Guan Yin but is often found in slightly different microclimates within the greater Anxi region.
processing: Ben Shan's leaves are thinner and more delicate than Tie Guan Yin's, making them best suited for light-handed processing. They develop their floral aroma quickly but cannot withstand heavy oxidation or roasting.
oxidation: Oxidation is kept very low (10-20%) to preserve its fresh, delicate, and high-pitched floral notes. The goal is to maximize the upfront aroma.
roasting: Almost never roasted, other than a final, low-temperature drying bake. Its delicate character would be completely overwhelmed by any significant roasting.
versatility: Not very versatile. It excels at one thing: being a light, fresh, and aromatic green-style oolong. It lacks the substance for traditional processing or for making other tea types.

name: Benifuki
description: 'Red Riches'. Japan's most famous and important black tea cultivar. It is a powerful hybrid of Assamica varieties, bred to produce a robust, full-bodied black tea with a strong astringency and notes of plum and citrus. It is also famous for its high content of methylated catechins, which are studied for their anti-allergic properties.

name: Benihikari
chineseName: べにひかり / 紅ひかり
description: 'Red Light'. A classic Japanese black tea cultivar with Darjeeling lineage, known for its muscatel-like aroma.

name: Bi Luo Chun Qunti
parentage: The native, seed-propagated heirloom population of the Dongting mountains.
description: 'Bi Luo Chun Population'. The original, small-leaf heirloom population from the Dongting mountains, famous for producing one of China's top ten green teas. The bushes are traditionally interplanted with fruit trees (like apricot, plum, and loquat), and the tea is said to absorb their fragrance. The finished tea consists of tiny, downy buds that are hand-rolled into a distinctive spiral shape.
plantType: Small, sprawling bushes with a less upright habit (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the unique microclimate of the Dongting peninsula on Lake Tai, where the lake effect moderates temperatures and the soil is ideal. Intercropping with fruit trees is key to the traditional terroir.
processing: The processing is incredibly laborious. The tiny, tender buds are pan-fired in a wok and simultaneously hand-rolled into their characteristic tight spiral shape. This requires immense skill to do without crushing the delicate buds.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The tea is pan-fired immediately after being picked to preserve its fresh, vibrant character.
roasting: No roasting. The pan-firing process serves to both kill-green and dry the tea.
versatility: Completely specialized. This heirloom cultivar is inextricably linked to the unique hand-processing and terroir of Dongting Bi Luo Chun.

name: Chin Hsin
parentage: (Jin Xuan x Qing Xin) x Cui Yu
description: 'Soothing Heart'. One of the newest cultivars released by TRES (2016), it was bred for broad appeal, combining the creamy texture of Jin Xuan with the elegant floral notes of Qing Xin. It is a modern, well-rounded cultivar designed for producing high-quality light oolongs.
plantType: Upright, vigorous bush with good yield.
environment: Adaptable to the mid-altitude oolong-producing regions of Taiwan.
processing: Processing aims to capture the best of both its parents, requiring careful withering to develop both the creamy and floral notes simultaneously.
oxidation: Undergoes light oxidation (15-30%) to maintain a fresh, aromatic profile.
roasting: Unroasted, to preserve the delicate balance of its creamy and floral characteristics.
versatility: Specialized for light oolongs. It was bred to be a high-quality, modern oolong and is not intended for other styles.

name: Cui Yu
parentage: TRES-2022 x Tainung #80
description: 'Jade'. Developed in 1981 by Taiwan's Tea Research and Extension Station (TRES), Cui Yu was bred for its powerful, unforgettable floral aroma. Often compared to magnolia and lily, it has become a cornerstone of modern Taiwanese oolongs, beloved for its high yield and fragrant character.
plantType: Early-sprouting, high-yielding arbor type (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis)
environment: Thrives in the misty, humid conditions of mid-to-high elevations (400-1,200m). Known for its vigor and good resistance to drought.
processing: Cui Yu's signature floral aroma is best expressed through controlled, light processing that emphasizes its natural aromatics over heavy-roast flavors.
oxidation: Typically undergoes light oxidation (15-30%) for oolongs. The extended withering process is crucial for developing its complex magnolia and gardenia notes.
roasting: Generally unroasted or receives a very light, low-temperature finishing roast for drying purposes. Heavy roasting can easily overwhelm its delicate floral bouquet.
versatility: It is a versatile cultivar. While ideal for light oolongs, careful full oxidation can produce a uniquely aromatic black tea that retains some of its floral heritage.

name: Da Hong Pao
description: 'Big Red Robe'. The most legendary and revered of all Wuyi Rock Oolongs. While the name refers to a few specific mother trees, most Da Hong Pao on the market is a masterful blend of other high-quality Wuyi cultivars (like Rou Gui and Shui Xian) made in the DHP style. It is the benchmark for the complex 'rock rhyme' (Yan Yun)—a unique mineral taste and texture derived from its rocky terroir.

name: Da Ye Zhong
parentage: The native, ancient tea varietal of Yunnan Province.
description: 'Big Leaf Variety'. This is not a single cultivar, but the broad-leaf botanical varietal, Camellia sinensis var. assamica, native to Yunnan. It is the genetic mother of all Yunnan tea and is known for its robustness, powerful flavor, and suitability for fermentation and aging. It is the raw material for both Pu'er and Dian Hong black tea.
plantType: Can grow into a large, ancient tree (gushu) or be cultivated as a bush (Camellia sinensis var. assamica).
environment: Thrives in the subtropical, mountainous, and biodiverse environment of Yunnan Province, with many distinct regional terroirs (e.g., Yiwu, Bulang, Lincang).
processing: This varietal's large, robust leaves are rich in polyphenols, making them ideal for the microbial fermentation of Pu'er tea and for creating complex, malty black teas. They can withstand significant processing.
oxidation: Oxidation varies dramatically by style. Sheng Pu'er is essentially an unoxidized (0%) sun-dried green tea. Dian Hong and Shu Pu'er are fully oxidized (100%).
roasting: Roasting is generally not a feature. Sheng Pu'er is sun-dried. Dian Hong is dried with hot air. Shu Pu'er is dried after its fermentation pile is complete.
versatility: Extremely versatile. As a foundational varietal, it is the basis for Yunnan's most famous and diverse tea styles, from green (Pu'er) to black (Dian Hong).

name: Da Yeh Oolong
parentage: Derived from Camellia sinensis var. assamica, brought from India.
description: 'Big Leaf Oolong'. This refers to a large-leaf Assamica varietal that has been cultivated in Taiwan for over a century. While not as famous for oolong as the small-leaf sinensis varieties, it can be crafted into a unique, full-bodied oolong. Its most important role, however, was as the genetic foundation for Taiwan's modern black tea breeding programs, including being a parent of Hong Yu #18.
plantType: Large, robust bush or tree with large, drooping leaves (Camellia sinensis var. assamica).
environment: Thrives in the hot, humid, and sunny low-altitude regions of eastern Taiwan.
processing: As an Assamica varietal, its leaves are rich in polyphenols, making them ideal for full oxidation. They are robust and can withstand heavy rolling to break down cell walls and encourage a strong, malty flavor.
oxidation: When made into black tea, it undergoes full oxidation (100%). When made into oolong, it requires heavy oxidation (50-70%) to tame its natural astringency.
roasting: No roasting. The tea is typically dried with hot air.
versatility: Primarily used for black tea. While it can be made into a niche oolong, its chemical composition and leaf structure are perfectly suited for producing strong, malty black tea.

name: Fo Shou
parentage: Brought from Yongchun, Fujian, China.
description: 'Buddha's Hand'. A large-leaf cultivar with origins in Yongchun, Fujian, that is also cultivated in Taiwan. It is named for its unusually large leaves, which resemble a Buddha's hand citron. In Taiwan, it is most famously used to create a distinct style of traditionally crafted, heavily roasted oolong in the Muzha area.
plantType: Large, sprawling bush with very large, broad, and dark green leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows well in the mid-elevation, humid environments of northern and central Taiwan.
processing: The large leaves of Fo Shou contain a lot of water and require a long, slow withering process. Their size and substance make them ideal for withstanding the stress of heavy oxidation and deep, slow roasting.
oxidation: Undergoes heavy oxidation (50-60%) to develop a deep, fruity, and honey-like flavor base that serves as the perfect canvas for roasting.
roasting: Very well-suited to heavy roasting. The traditional Muzha style involves multiple, slow bakes over charcoal, which builds immense depth, removes all astringency, and creates a signature caramel-like sweetness.
versatility: Specialized for traditional, heavily roasted oolongs. Its large leaf structure is not well-suited for light, 'green' oolong styles.

name: Fuding Da Bai
parentage: Selected from the native Fuding heirloom population for its large buds.
description: 'Fuding Big White'. The premier cultivar of Chinese white tea, Fuding Da Bai is the genetic backbone of the world's most famous white teas, including Silver Needle. It is celebrated for its large, fleshy buds that are covered in a thick layer of silvery-white down, which produce a tea that is exceptionally delicate, sweet, and clean.
plantType: Vigorous, large, early-sprouting bush with good cold resistance (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Prefers the mild, humid, and foggy coastal climate of Fuding, where the sea breezes and misty conditions are ideal for the slow withering process of white tea.
processing: The entire philosophy of processing this cultivar is minimalism. The goal is to preserve the natural state of the leaf with as little human intervention as possible. The thick, downy buds are key to its character.
oxidation: Oxidation is natural and very minimal (<5%), occurring slowly during the extended withering phase. There is no 'kill-green' step, allowing for a slight enzymatic change that develops its sweetness.
roasting: No roasting is involved. The tea is simply withered (in the sun or indoors depending on weather) and then gently dried at a low temperature to remove the final moisture.
versatility: Primarily specialized for white tea, where it is the undisputed champion. While it can be made into a simple black tea, its structure and flavor are best expressed through the gentle processing of white tea.

name: Goko
description: 'Enlightenment'. A classic and elite cultivar from Uji, Kyoto, Goko is one of the most important traditional cultivars for producing the highest grades of Gyokuro and Matcha. It is celebrated for its ability to develop an intense, profound, and savory 'umami' flavor when shaded, creating the archetypal 'brothy' character of Uji Gyokuro.

name: Gui Hua Xiang
parentage: One of the ten traditional fragrance types, selected from the native Phoenix Mountain population.
description: 'Osmanthus Fragrance'. A classic and beloved Phoenix Dan Cong oolong fragrance type. It is celebrated for its delicate, elegant, and very clear aroma of sweet osmanthus flowers. It is less overwhelmingly powerful than Mi Lan Xiang, offering a more refined and purely floral experience.
plantType: Medium-sized Dan Cong arbor (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the high-altitude, misty environment of the Phoenix Mountains, which allows for the slow development of its delicate aromatic compounds.

name: Hong Yu
parentage: C. sinensis var. assamica (Burma) x C. formosensis (Taiwanese Wild Tea)
description: 'Ruby'. Taiwan's most famous and unique black tea, Hong Yu is a modern hybrid developed by TRES. It is celebrated for its truly singular and powerful aroma, a complex bouquet of cinnamon, wintergreen, and mint, layered over a rich, malty base. It is a world-class black tea that has become an icon of the Taiwanese tea industry.
plantType: Vigorous, large-leaf bush with a strong upright growth habit.
environment: Prefers the warm, extremely humid, and stable climate around Sun Moon Lake, which mimics the conditions needed by its Assamica parentage.
processing: The processing is a relatively standard black tea method (wither, roll, oxidize, dry), but the magic is in the unique genetics of the leaf itself. The goal is simply to fully express the inherent character of the cultivar.
oxidation: Undergoes full and complete oxidation (100%) to develop the deep red color and the complex aromatic compounds that define it.
roasting: No roasting. The tea is dried with hot air to halt oxidation and reduce moisture content. All of its flavor comes from the leaf chemistry and oxidation.
versatility: Completely specialized. Hong Yu was bred for the express purpose of making a world-class black tea, and its unique genetics make it unsuitable for other styles.

name: Hong Yun
parentage: Indian 'Kyang' varietal x Keemun varietal
description: 'Red Rhyme'. Another modern black tea masterpiece from TRES, Hong Yun was developed to have a more fruit-forward and floral profile compared to Hong Yu's spicy character. It is known for its bright, uplifting aroma of citrus fruits like yuzu and orange peel, combined with a sweet, lingering floral finish.
plantType: Vigorous bush, slightly smaller and more compact than Hong Yu.
environment: Grows well in the warm, humid environment of Yuchi (Sun Moon Lake) and other black tea producing regions in Taiwan.
processing: Like Hong Yu, the processing is a standard black tea method. The skill of the tea master lies in perfectly timing the oxidation to capture the peak of its citrus and floral aromatics.
oxidation: Undergoes full oxidation (100%) to develop its bright red liquor and complex fruity-floral flavor profile.
roasting: No roasting. The tea is dried with hot air. Its flavor is derived from its unique parentage and the oxidation process.
versatility: Completely specialized. Hong Yun was specifically bred to create a unique, aromatic black tea and is not used for other tea styles.

name: Huang Guan Yin
parentage: Huang Dan (Huang Jin Gui) x Tie Guan Yin
description: 'Yellow Goddess'. A successful modern hybrid cultivar, created by crossing Huang Jin Gui (for aroma) and Tie Guan Yin (for substance). It is an intensely aromatic tea, often presenting a bouquet of powerful floral notes like gardenia and magnolia, and has become a popular 'new style' of Wuyi Rock Oolong.
plantType: Vigorous, productive, early-sprouting hybrid bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Bred to be vigorous and adaptable, it is grown in both Anxi and Wuyi. In Wuyi, the rocky terroir adds a mineral foundation to its powerful aroma.
processing: This cultivar was designed for aroma, so the entire processing chain is geared towards preserving its highly volatile floral compounds. Gentle handling is key.
oxidation: Oxidation is kept on the lighter side for an oolong (20-40%) to maintain the freshness and vibrancy of its floral character.
roasting: Roasting, especially for the Yancha style, must be very light and at a low temperature. It is more of a finishing bake to stabilize the tea. A heavy roast would completely destroy the delicate aroma it was bred to produce.
versatility: Moderately versatile. It can be crafted into either a Wuyi or Anxi style, but it will always be a light, intensely fragrant oolong. It lacks the structure for heavy roasting or black tea production.

name: Huang Jin Gui
parentage: Selected from the native Anxi heirloom population.
description: 'Golden Osmanthus'. A classic Anxi oolong celebrated for its singular, intense, and unmistakable aroma of sweet osmanthus flowers. It is an early-budding and high-yielding cultivar, prized for its ability to produce a light, crisp, and almost perfume-like tea that serves as a benchmark for pure floral aroma.
plantType: Early-budding, productive, spreading bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Thrives in the Hukou area of Anxi county, where the specific terroir is said to produce the most fragrant expression of the cultivar.
processing: The processing of Huang Jin Gui is a race against time to capture its volatile aromatics. The leaves are delicate and require gentle handling and a short processing window.
oxidation: Oxidation is very light (10-20%), just enough to eliminate the green, grassy notes and allow the powerful osmanthus fragrance to fully emerge.
roasting: Completely unroasted, aside from a final low-temperature bake for drying and stabilization. Any significant roasting would erase its signature character.
versatility: Not versatile at all. Huang Jin Gui is a master of a single craft: producing an intensely aromatic, light-bodied green oolong. Its entire value is based on this specialization.

name: Huangshan Qunti Zhong
parentage: The native, seed-propagated heirloom population of the Huangshan scenic area.
description: 'Huangshan Population'. The local, genetically diverse heirloom population of tea plants from the famous Huangshan (Yellow Mountain) scenic area. This is the authentic material for creating Huangshan Maofeng, a beloved green tea known for its light, sweet, and refreshingly floral character, often with notes of magnolia.
plantType: Variable growth habits due to genetic diversity; typically medium-sized bushes (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows at high altitudes (700-800m) in the cloudy, misty, and cool environment of Huangshan. The rich soil and constant cloud cover create a very sweet and tender leaf.
processing: The processing of Huangshan Maofeng is simpler than many famous teas. After a short withering, the leaves undergo a 'kill-green' and shaping process in a large pan, followed by a careful baking process to dry.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The 'kill-green' step is done quickly after harvest to lock in the fresh, vegetal and floral notes of the leaf.
roasting: The key step is a low-temperature bake ('hong bei'). Unlike the high heat of pan-firing, this gentle baking process slowly removes moisture while preserving the tea's delicate floral aroma and natural sweetness.
versatility: Completely specialized. This heirloom population is used exclusively to make the sweet, floral green tea known as Huangshan Maofeng.

name: Inzatsu 131
parentage: Assamica varietal x a native Shizuoka Zairai
description: An old and unique Japanese cultivar that is a hybrid of an Assamica variety and a native Zairai. It is known for its exotic, almost foreign aroma that is highly floral and sometimes spicy, reminiscent of teas from Darjeeling or Taiwan. It is a rare cultivar, prized by connoisseurs for its unique character.
plantType: Vigorous, semi-upright bush (Camellia sinensis hybrid).
environment: Well-suited to the climate of Shizuoka where it was developed.
processing: Processing Inzatsu 131 aims to highlight its unique, non-Japanese aroma. The method can be adapted to push it towards a greener or a more oxidized style depending on the tea maker's goal.
oxidation: Oxidation can vary. As a Sencha, it is unoxidized. However, it is often allowed a slight oxidation (like an oolong) to further develop its exotic floral and spicy notes.
roasting: Roasting is typically light to preserve its unique aroma.
versatility: Highly versatile. Its unique hybrid genetics make it a rare cultivar that can be successfully crafted into a wide range of styles, from a unique green tea to a fragrant oolong or black tea.

name: Jin Xuan
parentage: Ying Zhi Hong Xin x Tainung #8
description: 'Golden Lily'. A celebrated modern cultivar developed by Taiwan's TRES in 1981, it is famous for its distinct, natural 'nai xiang' or 'milk fragrance'. This creamy, buttery, and smooth profile, combined with its high yield and adaptability, has made Jin Xuan one of the most popular and beloved teas in Taiwan and beyond.
plantType: Vigorous, adaptable, high-yielding bush with distinctive round, thick leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Highly adaptable, thriving in a wide range of environments from lower elevations in Nantou to high altitudes on Alishan (200-1,600m).
processing: The processing for Jin Xuan oolong is specifically designed to highlight its unique, inherent 'nai xiang' (milk fragrance). Careful withering is key to developing this signature trait.
oxidation: For oolong, oxidation is light (15-25%) to preserve the creamy notes. For black tea, it undergoes full oxidation (100%), which transforms the creaminess into a honeyed sweetness.
roasting: Typically unroasted for the classic Milk Oolong style to maintain its fresh, creamy character.
versatility: Very versatile. It is a star performer as a light oolong and also makes an exceptionally smooth and sweet black tea, making it a valuable and flexible cultivar for farmers.

name: Ju Duo Zai
parentage: An old, native Phoenix Mountain varietal.
description: 'Saw-leaf'. A rare, old-grove Dan Cong varietal from the Phoenix Mountains, named for the sharply serrated, saw-like edges of its leaves. It is a rustic and powerful tea, known for its wild, herbal, and stone fruit character, representing an older, less-manicured style of Dan Cong.
plantType: Medium-sized Dan Cong arbor with distinctive, sharply serrated leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the old tea gardens of the Phoenix Mountains, often from trees that are quite old. The specific terroir contributes to its rustic and deep flavor.
processing: Processing this old-grove varietal follows traditional methods. The tea master aims to capture the full, complex character of the leaves rather than targeting a single, narrow fragrance profile.
oxidation: Undergoes a medium-to-heavy oxidation (40-55%) to develop its deep fruit notes and complex, rustic flavor base.
roasting: Typically receives a medium charcoal roast to integrate its powerful flavors, add depth, and ensure the tea will age well.
versatility: Highly specialized. Ju Duo Zai is a specific, old-style Dan Cong oolong appreciated for its rustic power and complexity.

name: Kanayamidori
description: A mid-budding cultivar known for its distinctive, slightly sweet, and milky or vanilla-like aroma. It is a popular choice for both Sencha and Fukamushi Sencha, and its unique fragrance also makes it a favorite for producing aromatic, lightly roasted Hojicha.

name: Kirari 31
parentage: 'Saemidori' x a hybrid of 'Sofu' and 'Makura-Cd86'.
description: A very new Japanese green tea cultivar registered in 2015. It was bred for its high resistance to disease and its suitability for producing a very fragrant and low-astringency Kamairicha (pan-fired green tea). It is known for its bright, clear liquor and a sweet, slightly milky, and floral aroma.
plantType: Early-budding, vigorous bush with excellent disease resistance (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Thrives in the warm climates of southern Japan, particularly in regions that specialize in Kamairicha production.
processing: Kirari 31 was specifically bred with pan-firing in mind. Its chemical composition responds well to the high, dry heat of this method, creating a fragrant tea without developing bitterness.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The 'kill-green' step, whether by pan-firing or steaming, is done immediately after harvest.
roasting: For its primary style, Kamairicha, the pan-firing serves as the 'roast', creating a gentle nutty character. For Sencha, it would receive a standard light final bake.
versatility: Moderately versatile. While it excels as a pan-fired tea, it can also produce a high-quality steamed Sencha, making it a valuable modern cultivar.

name: Komakage
parentage: Selected from a native Zairai population.
description: An excellent shading cultivar from Aichi prefecture, known for its strong, upright growth and resistance to cold. It produces a high-quality Tencha for Matcha with a good balance of umami and a unique, slightly savory, almost spicy character that distinguishes it from the classic Uji cultivars.
plantType: Vigorous, upright bush with strong cold resistance (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Very well-suited to the climate of Aichi and other regions that experience colder winters than southern Japan.
processing: Komakage is well-suited for shaded cultivation. Its robust nature makes it a reliable choice for farmers. It is processed into Tencha for Matcha production.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are steamed promptly after being harvested from the shaded plants.
roasting: No roasting. As Tencha, the leaves are dried flat in a special oven without being rolled to prepare them for stone-milling.
versatility: Highly specialized for Matcha. It is a key cultivar for Matcha production outside of the Uji region, particularly in Aichi.

name: Koshun
parentage: 'Kurizawa' x 'Kanayamidori'
description: 'Fragrance of Shizuoka'. A remarkable modern cultivar bred specifically for its astonishingly powerful and unique floral aroma. It produces a Sencha with a perfume-like fragrance reminiscent of lily-of-the-valley, jasmine, and cherry leaves, offering a completely different experience from classic, umami-focused Japanese green teas.
plantType: Upright, vigorous bush with long, elegant leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Well-suited to the climate of Shizuoka, where it was developed.
processing: Processing Koshun is all about capturing its volatile aromatic compounds. It is typically lightly steamed (Asamushi) to prevent the heat from damaging the delicate floral notes. Careful, low-temperature drying is also crucial.
oxidation: Zero oxidation for the Sencha style. The leaves are steamed immediately to lock in the floral aroma.
roasting: A very gentle, low-temperature final drying roast is used to avoid baking away the prized floral fragrance.
versatility: Moderately versatile. While its primary use is for a unique style of aromatic Sencha, its genetics also make it suitable for crafting fragrant Japanese oolongs.

name: Liu An Gua Pian
parentage: Local Qishan heirloom population ('Qishan Qunti Zhong').
description: 'Lu'an Melon Slice'. A unique and famous Chinese green tea from Anhui, notable for what it lacks: it is made entirely from mature leaves, with all buds and stems meticulously removed. The finished tea, resembling melon seeds, is baked, not pan-fired, giving it a complex, toasty, and vegetal flavor.
plantType: Hardy, medium-sized bushes from the local heirloom population (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the hilly, temperate climate of Lu'an City in western Anhui, particularly in the Qishan mountain range.
processing: The processing is unique. After picking, the leaves are de-stemmed and de-veined by hand. They are then wok-fired to kill-green and shape, followed by a multi-stage, slow baking process over charcoal fires, which is crucial for developing its flavor.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves undergo a rapid 'kill-green' in a wok to halt all enzymatic processes.
roasting: Roasting is the defining characteristic. The tea is baked multiple times over charcoal fires of varying intensity. This 'lao huo' (old fire) process builds a deep, complex, and toasty flavor without any smokiness.
versatility: Extremely specialized. This cultivar and its unique processing method (no buds/stems, baked) are inseparable from the identity of Liu An Gua Pian.

name: Long Jing #43
parentage: Selected and cloned from the native Long Jing Qunti Zhong population.
description: 'Long Jing No. 43'. The most widespread and commercially important modern cultivar for producing West Lake Long Jing tea. It was developed for its high yield, beautiful appearance, and early budding time, allowing for the prized pre-Qingming harvest. It produces the classic, beloved nutty and sweet soybean flavor of Long Jing.
plantType: Compact, early-sprouting bush with high productivity (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Thrives in the temperate climate and sandy loam soil of the hills surrounding Hangzhou's West Lake, though it is highly adaptable and grown elsewhere.
processing: Processing is defined by the pan-firing ('chao qing') step. The tender leaves are skillfully pressed against the hot surface of a wok to stop oxidation, dry the leaves, and shape them into their iconic flat form.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. As a green tea, the leaves are heated (in this case, pan-fired) almost immediately after harvesting to deactivate the enzymes responsible for oxidation.
roasting: No roasting. The 'roasty' notes in Long Jing come directly from the pan-firing process itself, not from a separate roasting step.
versatility: Specialized for pan-fired green tea. Its entire set of desirable traits—early budding, tender leaves, beautiful shape—is geared towards producing high-quality Long Jing.

name: Long Jing Qunti Zhong
parentage: The original, native heirloom population of the West Lake region.
description: 'Long Jing Population'. This is not a single clonal cultivar but the original, genetically diverse, seed-propagated heirloom population of Long Jing tea plants. Connoisseurs often prefer it to the modern #43 clone, believing it to have a deeper, more complex, and nuanced flavor profile, though its appearance is less uniform and it buds later.
plantType: Variable, seed-propagated bushes with diverse growth habits (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the core, traditional production areas around West Lake in Hangzhou. It is perfectly adapted to this specific terroir over centuries of growth.
processing: The processing is identical to Long Jing #43 (pan-firing), but the skill of the tea master is even more crucial due to the variability in leaf size and moisture content from the genetically diverse bushes.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. Like all Long Jing, it is a green tea where oxidation is halted immediately by pan-firing.
roasting: No roasting. The complex toasted notes are a direct result of the skillful pan-firing process.
versatility: Specialized for pan-fired green tea. It represents the historical and most complex expression of the Long Jing style.

name: Mao Xie
parentage: Distinct Anxi cultivar, not a direct Tie Guan Yin relative.
description: 'Hairy Crab'. An Anxi oolong cultivar named for the fine, downy hairs on its fresh leaves and the slightly curled shape of the brewed leaf, thought to resemble a crab. It is known for its forward, fruity-floral aroma, high yield, and early budding, making it a commercially important variety in Anxi.
plantType: Semi-spreading bush with dense branches and high productivity (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Highly adaptable and vigorous, growing well in the general terroir of Anxi County, from lower to mid-elevations.
processing: Mao Xie is prized for its upfront aroma which can be easily developed. The processing focuses on a controlled withering to bring out these volatile compounds without needing the heavy bruising or roasting that other cultivars require.
oxidation: Undergoes light oxidation (15-25%) to preserve its characteristic fresh and fruity notes. The processing is efficient and focuses on capturing the peak aroma.
roasting: Like Ben Shan, it is almost always unroasted or receives only a minimal drying bake to preserve its fresh, fragrant profile.
versatility: Similar to Ben Shan, it has low versatility. It is a specialist in producing fragrant, accessible, and affordable green-style oolongs and does not have the structure for other tea styles.

name: Mei Zhan
parentage: Originated in Anxi, Fujian.
description: A highly versatile Fujian cultivar, originally from Anxi. While it can be made into a pleasant oolong, it has gained modern fame as one of the primary cultivars used to produce Jin Jun Mei, an elite, bud-only black tea from the Wuyi region. Its inherent sweetness and fruity notes make it an excellent base for high-end black teas.
plantType: Vigorous, semi-arbor type with good adaptability (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Highly adaptable to different terroirs within Fujian, which has contributed to its widespread use.
processing: Mei Zhan's versatility is due to its balanced chemical composition. Its buds are particularly well-suited for black tea processing, as they are rich in compounds that create sweetness and a thick texture when fully oxidized.
oxidation: Oxidation is typically full (100%) for its most famous black tea expression. When made as an oolong, it undergoes medium oxidation (30-40%).
roasting: Roasting is not a key feature. Black tea expressions are simply dried. Oolong expressions may receive a light bake.
versatility: Extremely versatile. It is a rare cultivar that can be skillfully crafted into high-quality oolong, black, and even white tea, though its modern fame is overwhelmingly tied to black tea.

name: Meiryoku
description: A late-budding cultivar known for producing a Sencha with a refreshing, slightly floral aroma and a unique, bright flavor with hints of citrus and spice. It has a very favorable chemical composition with high amino acid content and is also noted for its strong resistance to common tea plant diseases.

name: Mengding Ganlu
parentage: Traditionally a local heirloom population; modern production often uses clones like 'Mengshan #9'.
description: 'Mengding Sweet Dew'. An ancient and celebrated green tea from Mengding Mountain in Sichuan, often cited as one of the oldest forms of tribute tea in China. It is known for its delicate, tightly rolled leaves covered in fine down, and a fresh, complex flavor profile that balances umami, sweetness, and a lasting floral aroma.
plantType: Small-leaf, downy-bud cultivar, adapted to high-altitude growth (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows on the perennially misty and rainy slopes of Mengding Mountain, where the constant cloud cover and rich soil create very tender and flavorful leaves.
processing: Processing involves a sequence of pan-firing to kill-green, followed by multiple stages of intricate hand-rolling and drying. This complex rolling technique is what creates the tightly twisted shape and develops the tea's deep flavor.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are quickly pan-fired after harvest to halt all oxidation.
roasting: No roasting. The tea is dried using the heat from the pan-firing and subsequent drying steps. The focus is on shape and preserving fresh flavor, not on a baked or roasted character.
versatility: Highly specialized. The cultivar is intrinsically linked to the Mengding Ganlu style of processed green tea.

name: Mengku Da Ye Zhong
parentage: A distinct local heirloom population of C. sinensis var. assamica.
description: 'Mengku Big Leaf Variety'. A highly sought-after sub-variety of the Da Ye (Assamica) varietal, native to the Mengku region of Lincang, Yunnan. It is celebrated for its 'dual characteristics' of strong bitterness and powerful aroma, combined with a thick texture and an exceptionally fast and intense returning sweetness ('huigan').
plantType: Large, robust arbor tree with large, leathery leaves that have prominent veins (Camellia sinensis var. assamica).
environment: Grows in the high-altitude, mountainous region of Mengku, particularly around Bingdao (Ice Island), which is famous for this cultivar.
processing: Processing is identical to other Sheng Pu'er teas: pan-firing to kill-green, rolling to shape, and crucially, sun-drying to preserve the enzymes necessary for long-term aging and fermentation.
oxidation: Minimal oxidation (<5%) from processing, just like other Sheng Pu'er. The true transformation happens over years of aging.
roasting: No roasting. Sun-drying is the defining and required final step before the tea is steamed and compressed into cakes.
versatility: Extremely specialized. The Mengku Da Ye cultivar is one of the most prized materials for high-end, single-origin Sheng Pu'er.

name: Mi Lan Xiang
parentage: A specific, highly successful fragrance-type selected from the local Shui Xian population.
description: 'Honey Orchid Fragrance'. The most popular, accessible, and representative of all Phoenix Dan Cong oolongs. It is beloved for its intoxicating and forward aroma that beautifully mimics the scent of honey, orchids, and ripe stone fruit, all built upon the classic mineral-rich foundation of its mountainous terroir.
plantType: Tall, upright arbor type, can grow into a small tree (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Thrives in the high-altitude (600-1,200m), misty, and rocky environment of the Phoenix (Feng Huang) Mountains.
processing: The key to processing Mi Lan Xiang is the carefully controlled withering and bruising ('yao qing') stage. This is where the leaf's cell walls are broken down just enough to develop the signature honey-orchid aroma without introducing bitterness.
oxidation: Undergoes a medium level of oxidation (25-40%), which is the sweet spot for developing its complex fruity and floral notes while retaining a fresh vibrancy.
roasting: Receives a light to medium charcoal roasting. This bake helps to stabilize the tea, round out the flavors, and fix the beautiful aroma, making it more persistent over multiple infusions.
versatility: Specialized for the Dan Cong oolong style. While theoretically it could be processed differently, its entire value and identity lie in its famous 'honey orchid' aromatic profile.

name: Oku Yutaka
description: 'Late Abundant'. A late-budding hybrid of Yabukita and Yutakamidori, Oku Yutaka combines the robust body of its parents with a refined, less astringent flavor. It is a high-yielding and disease-resistant cultivar, valued for producing a full-bodied Sencha with a rich flavor and a bright green color.

name: Okuhikari
parentage: Yabukita x a native Shizuoka Zairai
description: 'Late Light'. A late-budding cultivar with a refreshing, brisk mouthfeel and a distinct floral and woody character that sets it apart from the more common vegetal or umami-driven Senchas. It is a versatile and reliable cultivar for farmers.
plantType: Vigorous, late-budding bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Its late budding makes it a useful cultivar for extending the spring harvest season and avoiding frost. It is adaptable to various climates.
processing: Okuhikari is typically processed as a standard Sencha (Chumushi) to maintain the balance of its unique flavor profile.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are steamed immediately after harvest.
roasting: A standard light final drying roast is applied to stabilize the tea and round out its flavors.
versatility: Specialized for Sencha. It offers a unique flavor profile that adds diversity to the world of Sencha.

name: Okumidori
description: 'Late Green'. A late-budding, versatile cultivar with a rich, creamy flavor, often used for Matcha or blended with Yabukita.

name: Qi Lan
parentage: Originated in Pinghe County, southern Fujian.
description: 'Rare Orchid' or 'Marvelous Orchid'. A highly aromatic cultivar that originated in southern Fujian but has found a second home in the Wuyi Mountains. It is celebrated for its powerful and persistent orchid-like fragrance, which it can express beautifully as both a greener Anxi-style oolong and a more robust, roasted Wuyi-style rock oolong.
plantType: Upright, vigorous bush with good productivity (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Highly adaptable, it thrives in both the clay soils of its native southern Fujian and the rocky terroir of the Wuyi Mountains.
processing: it undergoes a traditional Yancha process with a moderate roast. In Anxi
oxidation: it is processed very lightly like a modern Tie Guan Yin to preserve its fresh aroma.,Oxidation ranges from light (20-30% for Anxi style) to medium (40-50% for Wuyi style)

name: Qi Men Zhong
parentage: The native, local heirloom population of Qimen county.
description: 'Qimen Species'. This is not a single clone, but the local heirloom population of small-leaf tea bushes from Qimen county, Anhui. It is the one and only material used for making Keemun black tea. When processed into black tea, it produces a famously complex aroma with notes of wine, rose, pine, and dried fruit, earning it the title 'the Burgundy of tea'.
plantType: Small-leaf, genetically diverse bushes adapted to the local terroir (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the mild, humid, and often foggy climate of Qimen county in southern Anhui, where the soil and environment are perfect for developing its complex aromatics.

name: Qing Xin
parentage: Brought to Taiwan from Fujian, China.
description: 'Green Heart'. The undisputed king of Taiwanese oolongs, Qing Xin is celebrated for its ability to perfectly express the unique terroir of Taiwan's high mountains. It produces a tea with an ethereal, elegant character, a remarkably thick and creamy mouthfeel, and a delicate floral aroma of lilac and gardenia. It is the benchmark for high-end Taiwanese tea.
plantType: Relatively small, slow-growing bush that requires meticulous care and specific conditions to thrive (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows best at very high altitudes (1,000-2,600m) where cool temperatures, constant mist, and large diurnal temperature swings concentrate flavors in the leaves.
processing: Processing Qing Xin is all about preservation. The goal is to capture the pristine character of the high-mountain leaf with minimal intervention. Gentle handling and a slow, controlled withering process are essential.
oxidation: Undergoes very light oxidation (15-25%) to develop its creamy texture and floral notes without losing the freshness endowed by its high-altitude terroir.
roasting: Generally unroasted. A final, very light bake is applied for drying, but any significant roast would be seen as masking the pure, delicate character of the leaf.
versatility: Highly versatile for high-quality teas. It is the gold standard for High Mountain Oolong and Baozhong, and also makes an excellent Taiwanese green tea. Its quality ceiling is extremely high.

name: Qing Xin Da Mao
altNames: Green Heart Big Hairy;Oriental Beauty Cultivar;Bai Hao Oolong Cultivar
parentage: Selected from native Chinese heirloom population.
description: 'Green Heart Big Hairy'. The indispensable cultivar for creating Taiwan's famous Oriental Beauty oolong. This tea's unique honey and muscat grape flavor is not from the leaf itself, but from its reaction to the bites of a tiny insect, the tea leafhopper. The cultivar's specific chemistry is perfectly suited to this remarkable transformation.
plantType: Sprawling, semi-upright bush, can be unruly (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Thrives in the hot, humid, and lower-altitude (100-400m) environments of northwestern Taiwan where the tea leafhopper (Jacobiasca formosana) is abundant.
processing: The entire process relies on nature; the tea must be bitten by the leafhopper. Processing then aims to highlight the resulting aromatic compounds. The leaves are handled gently to preserve their unique character.
oxidation: Undergoes heavy oxidation (60-70%), which is crucial for developing the complex honey and ripe fruit flavors that are created in response to the insect bites.
roasting: Completely unroasted. The rich, deep flavors are a result of oxidation, not heat. A finishing bake is used for drying only.
versatility: Extremely specialized. This cultivar's identity and value are entirely dependent on the presence of the tea leafhopper and the specific processing of Oriental Beauty oolong.

name: Qing Xin Gan Zhi
parentage: Selected from native Chinese heirloom population.
description: 'Green Heart Orange'. An older, traditional Taiwanese oolong cultivar that was more prominent before the widespread adoption of Qing Xin Oolong. It is known for producing a clean, fragrant, and slightly more vegetal Baozhong oolong and is a parent of the famous Si Ji Chun cultivar.
plantType: Semi-upright bush, considered a more 'rustic' cultivar (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Well-suited to the lower-altitude, humid basin environments like those found around Taipei.
processing: Processing is straightforward, following the traditional twisted-leaf Baozhong style. The goal is to preserve a fresh, green character.
oxidation: Undergoes very light oxidation (10-20%) to maintain its fresh, green, and floral notes.
roasting: Unroasted, aside from a final drying bake. Its delicate character is not suited for roasting.
versatility: Low versatility. It is a specialist for producing a classic, traditional style of Baozhong oolong.

name: Que She
parentage: A prized selection from the native Wuyi heirloom population.
description: 'Sparrow's Tongue'. A rare and highly sought-after Wuyi Rock Oolong named for its small, pointed leaves. It is celebrated for its exceptionally refined and elegant character, a high, sharp floral fragrance, and a very clean, mineral-driven taste. It is often processed with a lighter roast to preserve its delicate nature.
plantType: Small-leaf, slow-growing, semi-upright bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in specific, protected microclimates within the Wuyi Mountains. It is less common due to its lower yield and more demanding growing conditions.
processing: Processing Que She requires great finesse. The goal is to highlight its delicate, high-pitched aroma. The leaves, while small, are robust enough for Yancha processing but shine when handled with a lighter touch.
oxidation: Undergoes a standard medium oxidation (30-50%) to develop a base of flavor that supports, rather than overwhelms, its high-note aromatics.
roasting: Roasting is typically lighter than for other top-tier Yancha. A careful, low-temperature bake is used to bring out the mineral notes and add smoothness while preserving the vibrant floral fragrance.
versatility: Highly specialized. Que She is an expression of a more elegant and aromatic style of Wuyi Rock Oolong.

name: Rou Gui
description: 'Cassia/Cinnamon'. A top-tier Wuyi Rock Oolong prized for its pronounced spicy aroma. One of the most popular Yancha cultivars today.

name: Saemidori
description: 'Clear Green'. A modern elite cultivar prized for its vibrant color and low bitterness. A hybrid of Yabukita and Asatsuyu.

name: Samidori
description: A foundational and highly reliable cultivar from Uji, Kyoto. It is a versatile workhorse for the high-end shaded tea industry, particularly for Matcha. It is prized for its excellent, vibrant green color, good umami, and a smooth, well-balanced flavor that is ideal for creating both thick ('koicha') and thin ('usucha') Matcha.

name: Shi Da Cha
altNames: Persimmon Big Tea;Tai Ping Hou Kui cultivar
parentage: A local, large-leaf mutation of C. sinensis var. sinensis.
description: 'Persimmon Big Tea'. A truly unique and visually stunning cultivar from Taiping county in Anhui. It is defined by its massive leaves, which can be much larger than a person's hand. It is used exclusively to make Tai Ping Hou Kui, a green tea where the leaves are painstakingly pressed by hand, resulting in a long, flat, and beautiful finished product.
plantType: Large, robust bush with very strong branches to support its massive leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the misty, mountainous region of the former Taiping prefecture (now Huangshan district), where the specific microclimate allows these large leaves to grow tenderly.
processing: The processing is highly specialized and laborious. After kill-green, each individual leaf is placed between layers of cloth and hand-pressed with rollers to create its flat, uniform shape. This requires immense patience and skill.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The massive leaves are quickly pan-fired to halt enzymatic activity and preserve their vibrant green color and fresh aroma.
roasting: A gentle baking process follows the hand-pressing to slowly and evenly dry the large, thick leaves without scorching them or creating a roasted flavor.
versatility: Completely specialized. This unique, giant-leaf cultivar exists only to be made into the singular and iconic Tai Ping Hou Kui.

name: Shizu-7132
parentage: Natural mutation of Yabukita.
description: A famous un-registered cultivar from Shizuoka, renowned for its intense and unmistakable aroma of 'sakura-mochi'—a sweet, cherry blossom and glutinous rice scent. It is a natural mutation of Yabukita and offers a very popular and distinct aromatic experience.
plantType: Vigorous, mid-budding bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows well in Shizuoka and is prized by farmers who specialize in aromatic teas.
processing: Processing for 7132 is all about preserving its signature coumarin compound, which is responsible for the sakura aroma. This requires careful handling and specific steaming and drying parameters.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are steamed immediately after harvest.
roasting: A careful final drying roast is applied to enhance and fix the sweet, sakura-like aroma without creating any burnt notes.
versatility: Specialized for Sencha. Its entire value is based on its singular and highly sought-after cherry blossom aroma, so it is not used for other tea styles.

name: Shui Jin Gui
parentage: One of the four original, legendary Wuyi cultivars, with a famous origin story.
description: 'Golden Water Turtle'. Another of the four 'Si Da Ming Cong', this cultivar is steeped in a legend of being washed away by a flood and thriving in its new home. It is celebrated for its vibrant and highly fragrant character, striking a beautiful balance between bright, effusive floral notes (like gardenia and osmanthus) and the classic, creamy mineral base of a top-tier rock oolong.
plantType: Vigorous, productive bush with a semi-upright growth habit (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows well in the core production areas of the Wuyi Mountains, where the soil and climate help it develop its signature balance of aroma and texture.
processing: but not so much that it damages the delicate and valuable floral fragrance.,Highly specialized. Like its 'Si Da Ming Cong' siblings
oxidation: Shui Jin Gui is a singular expression of Wuyi Rock Oolong
roasting: valued for its unique and legendary aromatic profile.

name: Shui Xian
altNames: Water Sprite;Narcissus;Lao Cong Shui Xian (for old grove)
parentage: Selected from native Fujian heirloom population, likely originating in Jian'ou.
description: 'Water Sprite' or 'Narcissus'. A foundational Fujian oolong cultivar, famous for its versatility and profound transformation with age and processing. Young or lightly roasted Shui Xian is floral and bright, while heavily roasted or aged 'Lao Cong' (Old Grove) versions reveal deep, complex notes of aged wood, moss, and a resonant sweetness.
plantType: Versatile arbor type that can be a bush or a small tree (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis). Known for its large leaves.
environment: Highly adaptable. Thrives in the rocky terroir of Wuyi but also grows well in the clay soils of Southern Fujian. Old groves are in protected, high-humidity environments.
processing: Its large, robust leaves are highly forgiving and can withstand significant processing, whether it be the bruising of oolong production or the heavy oxidation of black tea. They are particularly well-suited to absorbing the character of a charcoal roast.
oxidation: Oxidation is highly variable, from a medium 30% for more floral styles to a heavy 60-70% for darker, more robust Yancha expressions that are destined for aging or heavy roasting.
roasting: Extremely responsive to roasting. This is the key variable that defines its style. Light roasting preserves its delicate floral notes, while multiple, heavy roasts build immense depth, complexity, and a smooth, woody character.
versatility: Highly versatile. Shui Xian is a master of transformation, capable of producing a wide spectrum of oolong styles from light and floral to dark and brooding. It also makes a respectable black tea.

name: Si Ji Chun
parentage: Natural cross-pollination of Wu Yi and Qing Xin Gan Zhi.
description: 'Four Seasons Spring'. A famously prolific and aromatic cultivar, discovered as a natural cross in the 1980s. It's named for its ability to be harvested almost year-round, while still producing a tea with an explosive, forward, and highly accessible floral aroma, primarily of gardenia and jasmine.
plantType: Extremely vigorous, dense, and highly productive bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Thrives in lower-altitude, warmer, and more humid climates, which allows for its near-constant flushing and harvesting.
processing: Processing is fast and efficient, aimed at capturing the cultivar's potent upfront aroma. It is a workhorse cultivar that responds well to standard green oolong processing.
oxidation: Oxidation is kept very light (10-20%) to ensure the final product is dominated by the fresh, powerful gardenia and jasmine notes.
roasting: Unroasted. Its value lies in its fresh floral aroma, which would be destroyed by any significant roasting.
versatility: Low versatility. While incredibly productive, it is a specialist in producing one type of tea: a fragrant, accessible, and affordable light oolong. It lacks the structure for other styles.

name: Sofu
parentage: 'Fuding Da Bai' x a native Saitama Zairai
description: 'Blue Wind'. A modern aromatic cultivar, similar to Koshun, that is prized for its striking and unique fragrance. It produces a Sencha or light oolong with a powerful perfume-like aroma of black currant, citrus, and mint, representing a new wave of aromatic Japanese teas.
plantType: Vigorous, upright bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Adaptable to various climates, it is a key cultivar for the Saitama region.
processing: Like other aromatic cultivars, Sofu is processed with a gentle hand to preserve its volatile compounds. Light steaming is preferred to avoid damaging the unique aroma.
oxidation: Zero oxidation for the Sencha style. Steamed immediately after harvest.
roasting: A very light final drying roast is applied to stabilize the tea without diminishing its powerful, unique fragrance.
versatility: Moderately versatile. It is primarily used for creating unique aromatic Senchas and is also an excellent choice for making Japanese-style light oolongs.

name: Song Zhong
parentage: The original mother tree of all Dan Congs, said to have been growing since the Song Dynasty.
description: 'Song Dynasty Cultivar'. The apex predator of Phoenix Dan Cong oolongs, Song Zhong refers to teas made from the direct descendants of the oldest known tea tree on Wudong Mountain (reputed to be over 600 years old). It is an incredibly powerful, deep, and complex tea, known for its profound 'cha qi' (tea energy) and a layered flavor profile that can only be achieved through great age and perfect terroir.
plantType: Old, gnarled, and often moss-covered arbor trees with highly variable leaf shapes (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows exclusively on Wudong Mountain, the highest peak in the Phoenix range, in mineral-rich, yellowish-brown soil at very high altitudes (>1100m).
processing: Processing tea from such old trees is an immense responsibility. The tea master must use all their skill to translate the raw potential of the leaves into a finished tea that is worthy of its lineage. The process is slow, careful, and traditional.
oxidation: Undergoes a deep and complex oxidation process (can be 40-60% or more) that is carefully monitored to develop its multi-layered aromatic profile.
roasting: The roasting is deep, slow, and done in multiple stages over charcoal. This complex roasting process is essential for integrating the tea's powerful flavors, smoothing its texture, and creating a tea that will continue to age and improve for years.
versatility: The ultimate specialist. Song Zhong represents the highest achievement of the Dan Cong oolong style and is never made in any other way.

name: Taiwanese Wild Tea
parentage: Native, indigenous species to Taiwan.
description: The native, indigenous tea species of Taiwan, genetically distinct from the more common Camellia sinensis. It grows wild in the central mountain range. While not a major commercial crop, it is wild-harvested for specialty teas and is crucially important as genetic stock for breeding, most famously as a parent of the Hong Yu #18 'Ruby' cultivar.
plantType: Wild-growing tree that can become very large and old (Camellia formosensis).
environment: Grows wild in the protected, biodiverse forests of Taiwan's central mountain range at various altitudes.
processing: Processing is often experimental and done by boutique producers. The wild-harvested leaves are precious and are typically handled with care to express their unique, wild character.
oxidation: Typically undergoes full oxidation to be made into black tea, which seems to best complement its wild, woody, and herbaceous notes.
roasting: No roasting. The tea is dried with hot air.
versatility: Not a commercial production cultivar, but a specialty item and a vital genetic resource. It is a wild plant, not a cultivated one in the traditional sense.

name: Takachiho
parentage: Selected from a native Zairai population.
description: A classic cultivar specific to the regions in Kyushu that specialize in 'Kamairicha' or pan-fired green tea. It is prized for its ability to withstand the high heat of pan-firing, producing a green tea with a beautiful nutty and roasted aroma ('kama-ka') that is very different from the vegetal notes of steamed Sencha.
plantType: Medium-sized, robust bush adapted to pan-firing (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Thrives in the warm climate of southern Kyushu, particularly Miyazaki, the heart of Kamairicha production.
processing: the leaves are fired in a hot iron pan or rotating drum
oxidation: a technique originally from China. This high
